limits: Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.

Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.

Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.

Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.

name: fft
notes: Frequency-domain suite, function fft (brief 148). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal properties and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement on LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power exists because none has been measured; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml, queued in _handoff/fpga_agent/vivado_later_queue.md) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. There are no Lean statements and no packaged harness for this suite (stated in the report). item_views.title: Worst error against NumPy at every recorded point (the record of the last run)

missing_methods: a simulation check from a bench the implementing agent did not write
requirements.text: For each variant, scaling mode and several N and twiddle widths, the error of the model (which the RTL equals bit for bit) against the double-precision FFT of NumPy is recorded in verif/results/accuracy.json: worst and rms error in units of the output LSB, and the SQNR and SFDR for a full-scale tone. The recorded worst error of the scaled mode is at most 6 LSB at every recorded point, and the unscaled mode's SQNR for noise-like input is at least 80 dB at every recorded point with twiddles of 16 bits or more (the unscaled word is W + LOGN bits wide, so its error in output LSBs is large for narrow twiddles: the SQNR is the figure to read); these are the bounds the test enforces, and the figures are what the report states, with no claim beyond them.
requirements.title: Accuracy against NumPy's FFT is measured and stated, per scaling mode
